Items.Authors: Christoph Tenzer, Christine Kopik, Joerg Bayer, Andrea Santangelo, Gabriel Cobos Tello, David Blanquez Sese, Irfan Kuvvetli, Luca Bune Jensen, Claudio Labanti, Enrico Virgilli, Denis Tcherniak
Items.Title: The THESEUS/XGIS digital data processing architecture: from detection to trigger
Items.Abstract: The X- and Gamma-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XGIS) on board THESEUS is a wide-field coded-mask camera system formed by two identical, partially overlapping imagers. It provides accurate sky imaging over a 2-steradian field of view in the 2-150 keV band, together with timing and spectroscopic coverage up to several MeV. Each imager comprises 10 SuperModules, further divided into Modules hosting 64 Silicon Drift Detector pixels coupled to CsI(Tl) scintillator bars for combined X-ray and gamma-ray detection.    This poster presents the higher-level digital data-processing chain implemented in the XGIS Camera Back-End Electronics and the XGIS Instrument Data Handling Unit (I-DHU), including event sorting, image deconvolution, light-curve and photon-list generation, and the execution of image-, rate-, and MEPSA-based trigger algorithms for rapid transient detection and localization.

Items.Authors: Simonetta Chinellato, Joseph Huesler, Natalia Auricchio, Timothy Bandy, Francesco Borsa, Alexis Brandeker, Daniele Brienza, Flavia Calderone, Virginie Cessa, Jacopo Farinato, Mauro Ferrero, Federico Iotti, Emanuele Macri, Demetrio Magrin, Luca Marafatto, Massimo Marinai, Matteo Munari, Marco Nebiolo, Stefano Nocentini, Andrea Novi, Roberta Orsi, Isabella Pagano, Daniele Piazza, Raffaele Piazzolla, Giovanni Postiglione, Roberto Ragazzoni, Giammarco Roini, Filippo Ruggiero, Mario Salatti, Elia Sardi, Elisabetta Tommasi, Donata Valletti, Valentina Viotto
Items.Title: The TOU within the PLATO mission: aspects of product assurance leading to the identification of lessons learned
Items.Abstract: PLATO, the ESA M3 mission, currently almost wholly integrated and under final verification and validation, is planned to be launched in the beginning of 2027. PLATO is composed by 26 Cameras, each including a Telescope Optical Unit (TOU), i.e. the opto-mechanical unit. Developing 26 TOU Flight Models (FM) has been a recurring and extensive work for the delivery of such a high number of telescopes.   Not many missions have a series production, the repeating of the same procedures, from a Product Assurance point of view, gives the possibility to increase the quality of the activities and workmanship on the subsequent models. Nevertheless, discrepancies from requirements and non conformities have been found also in the latest models. We will present which are the most common discrepancies and which are surprisingly new, giving an overall view of the lessons learned.

Items.Authors: Matthew Taylor, Patrick Côté, Tyrone Woods, John Pazder
Items.Title: The vacuum ultraviolet laboratory (VUVLab) at the University of Calgary
Items.Abstract: The Vacuum UltraViolet Laboratory (VUVLab) at the University of Calgary is a unique facility designed to test and characterize ultra-violet and blue-optical sensitive detectors under high vacuum conditions. The VUVLab was previously used to characterize the UV photon-counting device on the UltraViolet Imaging Telescope aboard the AstroSat mission and has been receiving upgrades ahead of broadscale testing of a CIS120 CMOS device to support the upcoming CASTOR space telescope mission. The VUVLab is versatile in that it features a ~500 litre vacuum vessel that contains a five axis (three translational, two rotational) manipulator unit that allows easy translation of the detector across the UV beam. In this talk, I will summarize recent upgrades to the VUVLab and its current capabilities. A summary of tests on a CIS120 CMOS device will be provided, as well as future plans to make the VUVLab a world-class generalized UV detector testing facility.

Items.Authors: Martina Torsello, Marcella Massardi, Elisabetta Liuzzo, Gayathri Gururajan, Francesca Perrotta, Andrea Lapi
Items.Title: The ViSta method for optimized stacking of broadband interferometric data in the Fourier domain
Items.Abstract: We present the optimized version of ViSta, a visibility-domain stacking method that combines interferometric observations in the Fourier domain from radio to sub-millimeter wavelengths. By stacking visibilities directly and transforming them into the rest frame, ViSta enhances the signal, suppresses noise, and improves image reconstruction through extended uv-coverage. The method is highly flexible, allowing stacking regardless of array configuration, spectral setup, or telescope. Its uv-plane approach offers a parallelizable and highly optimizable framework suited for scalable and cross-facility integration. We show that ViSta outperforms image stacking when individual sources are too faint to detect, achieving higher SNR in the low-signal and extended regime. In the SKA era, where visibilities will not be routinely preserved, ViSta helps in assessing the information lost in the image-plane transition and in exploiting the vast amount of data still stored in interferometric archives.

Items.Authors: Francisco Javier Veredas, Sebastian Albrecht, Robert Andritschke, Benjamin Mican, Monika Zuchniak, Konrad R. Skup, Jarosław Borek, Denis Tcherniak, Gabriel Cobos Tello, Carol Anne Oxborrow, Irfan Kuvvetli, Jens Loehring, Harald Jeszenszky, Johan Hasiba, Harald Ottacher, Gunter Laky, Gabriel Giono, Marko Mecina, Roland Ottensamer, Jorge Lucio Tonfat Seclen, Kirpal Nandra, Nikhil More, Tayyaba Suleman, Hadil Hajri, Elif Kutdemir Öncü
Items.Title: The WFI Instrument Control Unit for the ESA NewAthena mission
Items.Abstract: We present the Instrument Control Unit for the WFI NewAthena instrument in its current phase (ESA Phase B1). The ICU manages the complete WFI instrument and interfaces to the spacecraft on-board-computer (OBC). ICU electronics prototypes have been built and the first test results have been obtained. The viability of the ICU for the adoption of the NewAthena mission and development in later phases can be noted.

Items.Authors: Riccardo Campana, Alfonso Pisapia, Farangis Takdehghan, Lorenzo Amati, Enrico Virgilli, Claudio Labanti, Paolo Calabretto, Giulia Mattioli, Smiriti Srivastava, Ajay Sharma, Sandro Mereghetti, Edoardo Arrigoni
Items.Title: The XGIS instrument on-board THESEUS: the simulated response and background
Items.Abstract: The behaviour and performance of the X and Gamma Imaging Spectrometer (XGIS) instrument onboard the Transient High Energy Sky and Early Universe Surveyor (THESEUS) mission, currently under ESA assessment within the Cosmic Vision M7 programme, has been thoroughly investigated through detailed simulations carried out with a Geant4-based Monte Carlo framework using an updated mass model. This work outlines the main contributions to the instrumental background expected in the Low Earth Orbit planned for THESEUS, including diffuse photon fields, various cosmic-ray components, and Earth albedo radiation. The resulting simulated in-orbit background conditions, together with their impact on the overall response and sensitivity of the instrument, are also presented.

Items.Authors: Xiaosong Wu
Items.Title: Theoretical and experimental research on computational synthetic aperture wavefront sensing
Items.Abstract: Computational synthetic aperture wavefront sensing (CSA-WFS) extends the principles of Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensing by computationally fusing multiple subaperture images into a single, synthetically enlarged subaperture. This approach emulates the signal characteristics of a larger subaperture, thereby significantly enhancing the spot signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) without compromising spatial sampling density. By decoupling SNR from subaperture size, CSA-WFS overcomes the traditional trade-off between SNR and spatial resolution inherent in conventional Shack–Hartmann designs. The method offers dynamically tunable performance, enabling real-time optimization of wavefront sensing fidelity across varying observing conditions. Guided by theoretical analysis, we have successfully implemented CSA-WFS on both solar and astronomical telescopes. Experimental results confirm its superior capability in detecting faint wavefront signals, substantially broadened detection bandwidth.

Items.Authors: Anirudh Mukund Saraf, Valeria Antonelli, Kirpal Nandra
Items.Title: Thermal design and control of Wide Field Imager on NewAthena X-ray space telescope
Items.Abstract: The Wide Field Imager (WFI) is one of the two instruments on the NewATHENA X-ray observatory, designed for high-throughput imaging and spectroscopy. This paper presents the current status of WFI thermal design, covering the Camera Head Subsystem, the Primary Structure Subsystem with the Filter Wheel, the Detector Electronics Units and the Instrument Control Units. For the first time, the thermal behaviour has been evaluated for multiple Filter Wheel positions, assessing their impact on detector and electronics temperatures and stability, as well as the resulting heat load at the WFI thermal interfaces. The study outlines key design challenges, analysis methodology, and temperature and heat load results across all instrument configurations.

Items.Authors: Benjamin Gonzalez Barraza, Nicolas Hernandez, Sylvain Cetre, Esteban Vera, Benoit Neichel
Items.Title: Towards a real-time adaptive optics controller for deep learning wavefront sensors
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) is a key technology for the next generation of extremely large telescopes and laser-based satellite communication links, where diffraction-limited performance must be preserved under strong, varying atmospheric turbulence. Deep-learning wavefront sensors promise higher reconstruction accuracy but must run at kilohertz rates with sub-millisecond latency to keep residual wavefronts nearly static. We present a real-time control architecture that couples Neural Networks (NNs) optimized with TensorRT to the Durham Adaptive Optics (DAO) shared-memory framework. By keeping camera frames, control parameters, and deformable-mirror commands in GPU memory, we minimize data transfers and allow all pre/post-processing to run on GPU. We demonstrate experimental closed-loop AO on the PULPOS bench with several NNs, achieve our first on-sky results on PAPYRUS at OHP (France), and are pursuing further optimization and new on-sky tests at the SEETRUE Optical Ground Station in Chile.

Items.Authors: Kyliann Robert, Cyril Petit, Perrine Lognoné, Aurélie Montmerle-Bonnefois, Nicolas Védrenne, Thierry Fusco
Items.Title: Towards experimental validation of LQG-based predictive control for PAA precompensation of GEO feeder optical links
Items.Abstract: Going towards predictive AO control for ground-to-GEO optical telecommunication links, we want to implement the static prediction method presented in Perrine Lognoné's PhD thesis. It uses phase and intensity measurements of the downlink path to compute a pre-compensation to apply on the uplink path. From this static method, we study the derivation of an LQG-based real-time controller for dynamic correction computation. Will be presented theoretical and numerical aspects, such as the structure of this controller taking phase and intensity as inputs, end-to-end simulations, as well as experimental design considerations for laboratory testing, and intensity calibration of the wavefront sensor, all towards the first laboratory experiment.

Items.Authors: Talon Myburgh
Items.Title: Towards maximizing the SETI discovery space via targeted imaging with radio interferometers
Items.Abstract: Breakthrough Listen’s SETI surveys typically use radio antenna arrays and beamforming to achieve peak sensitivity toward pre-selected targets. However, this limits the observable parameter space of detected signals and hinders discrimination between signals of anthropogenic origin and potential extraterrestrial signals. While real-time synthesis imaging of a full observation is currently intractable, this research focuses on generating small, high-resolution "postage stamp" images of all signals detected by the conventional beamforming technique. This provides spatial and polarisation information, albeit over a reduced temporal and frequency range. Enabled by GPU acceleration and Nvidia’s Holoscan framework, this targeted imaging approach aims to run in real-time and extend the scientific utility of SETI data. While currently focused on small image regions, this research lays a foundation for a full observation real-time imaging pipeline necessary for next-generation SETI research.

Items.Authors: Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta, Sebastiano Ligori, Anna Maria Di Giorgio, Pierpaolo Merola, Marina Vela Nuñez, Marianna Michelagnoli, Mauro Focardi
Items.Title: Towards the definition of flight operation procedures for the ARIEL Instrument Control Unit
Items.Abstract: ARIEL, ESA’s M4 mission launching in 2031, aims to chemically characterise about one thousand exoplanet atmospheres through low-resolution transit spectroscopy using the AIRS (ARIEL IR Spectrometer) and the Fine Guidance Sensor (FGS). Within this context, dedicated Flight Operations Procedures (FOPs) are being developed for the Instrument Control Unit (ICU), which controls AIRS and the Telescope Control Unit (TCU). These structured and traceable procedures support instrument operations from integration and verification to in-flight use. Their development builds on the Full Functional Tests (FFTs), a set of TCL scripts used to verify requirements. The methodology identifies atomic scripts as building blocks for the FOPs, later converted into procedure-management formats for the final implementation of the needed services in the ICU Application Software, including those needed for the FDIR (Fault Detection, Isolation and Recovery).

Items.Authors: Chi H. Nguyen
Items.Title: Tracing the boundary of the South Atlantic Anomaly region with SPHEREx transient flagging rates
Items.Abstract: The NASA SPHEREx satellite was launched in 03/2025 to survey the full sky between 0.75 - 5.0 um. The image processing of SPHEREx H2RG detectors includes real-time flagging of transient events during integration. SPHEREx follows a polar orbit passing over the South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) zone multiple times daily, where the transient counts reach as high as >80% of pixels, depleting the pixel inventory for further calibration. The science pipeline flags for re-observation all exposures taken while in the SAA, as well as any with >10% transients regardless of the spacecraft location. After six months, ~1.5% of the exposures outside of the pre-defined SAA zone were flagged. Most are near the poles; but also adjacent to the edges of the SAA, potentially expanding its boundary. Given the importance of the SAA to designing and operating space instruments, we present here the SAA boundary traced by SPHEREx transient flags as a reference for future missions.

Items.Authors: Lucie Leboulleux, Raphaël Pourcelot, Laurent A. Pueyo
Items.Title: Trade-off between segment density and coronagraph design in high-contrast Exoplanet imaging: evaluating sensitivity to phasing errors in large segmented space missions
Items.Abstract: To image Earth-like exoplanets, coronagraphs on future segmented space telescopes like the Habitable Worlds Observatory must reach contrasts of 10^-10 at separations below 100 mas, requiring picometer-level segment phasing control. We explore how relaxing this constraint is possible by optimizing system parameters such as primary mirror segmentation and focal-plane mask (FPM) size. We assess both passive robustness to phasing errors and the effectiveness of a Zernike low-order wavefront sensor in correcting them. Our results show that increasing the FPM radius or reducing the number of segments improves high-contrast stability and wavefront sensing performance.

Items.Authors: Isabel J. Kain, John O'Meara, Marc Kassis, Antonin Bouchez, Peter Wizinowich, James Lyke, Avinash Surendran, Imke de Pater, Katherine de Kleer, Ned Molter, Steph Sallum, Rosalie McGurk, Andy Skemer
Items.Title: Twilight observing with SCALES on Keck: science program and projected performance
Items.Abstract: Twilight presents an opportunity for infrared astronomers: while the brightening sky closes the observing window for optical astronomers, the infrared sky does not significantly brighten even through sunrise. The Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) instrument is a 1-5µm imager and 2-5µm integral field spectrograph currently being commissioned at Keck Observatory, which will execute a twilight science program that expands on the successes of the extant Twilight Zone program with NIRC2 and OSIRIS. This paper presents an optimized and executable SCALES twilight program, prioritizing (1) monitoring of Solar System objects to study time-domain phenomena and support future NASA missions, and (2) support transiting exoplanet discovery by conducting direct imaging follow-up of TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs). We describe the science program along with optimized observing configurations and report preliminary results from SCALES commissioning.

Items.Authors: Richard C. Y. Chou, Shiang-Yu Wang, Po-Chieh Yu, Yuhei Takagi, Yosuke Minowa, Shin Oya, Yoshito Ono, Hirofumi Okita
Items.Title: Ultimate-Subaru: design of the optical test platform for the calibration process of the adaptive secondary mirror and the wave front sensor
Items.Abstract: We present the optical and opto-mechanical design for the test system of the adaptive secondary mirror of the ULTIMATE-Subaru project, which is the next-generation facility instrument for the Subaru Telescope. A test tower will be used to evaluate the surface of the mirror, and an optical platform is designed and installed on this tower to test the function of both the adaptive secondary mirror and the wavefront sensor. The detailed optical and opto-mechanical design of the optical platform will be described.

Items.Authors: Jonathan Dray, Morgan Gray, Baptiste Sinquin, Jalo Nousiainen, Cédric Taïssir Héritier Salama, Hisham Forriere, Julien Charton, Armin Schimpf, Thierry Fusco, Benoit Neichel
Items.Title: U-net based reconstruction coupled with reinforcement learning for adaptive optics in LEO optical links
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present a reconstruction pipeline for LEO satellite free-space optical communications, combining a U-Net–based deep learning reconstructor with the predictive PO4AO controller. We show that the U-Net outperforms classical reconstruction methods under low-photon-flux and high-scintillation conditions. Closed-loop simulations at kilohertz rates demonstrate improved fiber coupling efficiency compared to classical Karhunen–Loève reconstruction, across varying elevation angles and Rytov variances. This approach highlights the benefit of integrating deep learning upstream of model-based predictive control for challenging adaptive optics scenarios.

Items.Authors: Natasha Popenoe, Benjamin L. Gerard, Dominic Sanchez
Items.Title: Update on the fastrSHWFS
Items.Abstract: Adaptive Optics (AO) system bandwidth error has been shown to be the dominant error term limiting exoplanet imaging detection sensitivity. We have proposed a solution to improve Shack Hartman wavefront sensor (SHWFS) bandwidth error called the fastrSHWFS, using a custom lenslet array mask to redistribute subapertures from an input circular pupil into a linear or rectangular geometry on the WFS detector to decrease camera read time and thus reduce bandwidth error. In past work fabricated fastrSHWFS lenslet masks had insufficient optical quality; here we present simulation and testing results of new fastrSHWFS masks made by a recently available greyscale two photon polymerization 3D printing technology that in principle provides sufficient depth resolution and dynamic range for such masks.   This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under Contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. This document number is LLNL-ABS-2014298.

Items.Authors: Danièl N. Groenewald, Kenneth Nordsieck
Items.Title: Updated polarimetric calibration model for SALT RSS: addressing waveplate-dependent pupil asymmetry
Items.Abstract: We present an update to the polarimetric calibration of the Southern African Large Telescope’s Robert Stobie Spectrograph (RSS) to resolve a remaining modeling inadequacy. Polarimetric pupil imaging taken with RSS shows a waveplate pupil asymmetry rotating with the waveplate angle, and this is modelled only approximately in the current calibration. This asymmetry is not present in perfectly-manufactured panchromatic waveplates, and it must be included accurately for accurate calibration.

Items.Authors: Patrick Caillier, Florian Kerber, Sebastian Egner, Eric Emsellem, Markus Schoeller, Mauro Tuti, Elena Liopis, Herve Kurlandczyk, Adeline Fesquet, Sergio Gonzales, Frederic Gonte, Vittorio Nurzia, Robert Hamilton, Susana Rodriguez
Items.Title: Updating ESO’s project management framework
Items.Abstract: ESO’s Mission is to design, build and operate advanced ground-based observatories, and to foster international collaboration for astronomy. ESO has a dedicated Project Management Department (PMD) with more than 20 staff providing the expertise and leadership on projects. Traditionally, the focus has been on major hardware and infrastructure projects such as telescopes and instruments. Recently the project portfolio has been becoming more diverse encompassing projects with significant software components and various change management projects. With the construction of the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) has entered the domain of “big science” and with the “Expanding Horizons” initiative ESO and its community are already looking towards the next project that will transform astronomy in the 2040s. ESO’s PMD is in the process of updating its PM framework to reflect these developments in order to prepare for future challenges in close cooperation with other organisational units.

Items.Authors: Roberto Abuter, Federico Pellegrin, Babak Sedghi, Luis Esteras, Saul Menendez, Julien Woillez, Mario Kiekebusch, Matthew MacIntosh
Items.Title: Upgrade of the VLTI vibration system using low-noise accelerometers with digital EtherCAT interface
Items.Abstract: A new vibration monitoring and control system is presented for the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) Unit Telescopes to replace the legacy architecture now limited by sensor noise and by the analog signal transmission network. The new system is based on low-noise EtherCAT accelerometers selected and adapted for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) and employs a fully digital acquisition and transmission chain to eliminate analog links and reduce electromagnetic interference. A Beckhoff PLC operates as EtherCAT master, while a Linux workstation receives data via a deterministic UDP link using the Messaging UDP Interface (MUDPI) protocol. System architecture, integration, and estimated performance are presented.

Items.Authors: Nelly Natalia Cerpa Urra
Items.Title: Using adaptive optics for FSO communication for fiber coupling: first results of a free space onground link at Uandes
Items.Abstract: This presentation explores the possibilities of using AO,widely applied to the correction of turbulent phases in astronomy but now used in free-space communications (FSO). Optimal controllers have been demonstrated to be a helpful way of improving the error budget on extremely demanding AO systems in astronomy. Still, no recent study shows the full benefits of implementing an optimal control AO in a working FSO communication system. Here, we not only present our first results after implementing a closed-loop AO system bench at the Universidad de los Andes laboratory, we also present first results for the application of AO for optical coupling using a 1-km laser on ground link at Universidad de los Andes. We present control optimization strategies and future plans for the AO system at a 4-km link.

Items.Authors: Ugo Tricoli, Cèdre Mercier, Romain Fétick, Eric Coiro, Yannick Abautret, Alisson Pellissiere, Josselin Defrance, Yves-Michel Frédéric, Nicolas Védrenne, Thierry Fusco, Jean-François Sauvage, Cyril Petit
Items.Title: Using SIRIUS to simulate space/ground telescope observations of satellites, debris and asteroids from the visible to the thermal IR
Items.Abstract: Tracking of satellites, debris and asteroids is essential for space operations. Optical detection from space or ground telescopes offers an interesting alternative to radars. We developed at ONERA a software called SIRIUS (Simulateur InteRactif d’Images Ultra Spectrales) to simulate and predict these kind of observations. High spatial and spectral resolution calculations of the visible/IR signature of different targets from 0.3 µm to 14 µm can be performed. The calculation is optimized through parallelization of the ray tracing on the GPU. The paper will study theoretically the gain of information related to a spatially resolved or non-resolved (light-curves) optical detection from a ground or space telescope in order to understand the benefits given by the mixed use of visible and thermal IR bands (the LWIR in optics or the mid-IR N-band in astronomy). Simulations examples will be given for space/ground observations of different satellites, debris and asteroids.

Items.Authors: Sara Leardini
Items.Title: Using X-Ray Fluorescence to characterise lunar regolith with focus on light elements
Items.Abstract: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) enables elemental analysis through characteristic X-ray emissions and is well suited for studying lunar regolith, a fine, abrasive, electrically charged dust that poses major challenges for future missions. Traditional APXS instruments rely on ²⁴⁴Cm sources, which are difficult to procure and handle and may damage instrumentation due to high alpha activity. Recent advances in detector window materials allow the use of more accessible sources such as ⁵⁵Fe and ¹⁰⁹Cd. In this work, we present the experimental setup designed for regolith XRF analysis, with focus on light elements such as oxygen. Results from simulations and laboratory tests demonstrate the feasibility of replacing alpha-induced fluorescence with safer and more practical sources, supporting the development of robust XRF instruments for upcoming lunar missions.

Items.Authors: Athira Unni, Steph Sallum, Andy Skemer, Peyton Benac, Rosalie McGurk, Max Brodheim, William T. S. Deich, Michael P. Fitzgerald, Richard Deno Stelter, Mackenzie Lach, Isabel J. Kain
Items.Title: Validating the SCALES DRP: A Performance Study of the Medium-Resolution IFS Mode
Items.Abstract: We present performance verification of the medium-resolution IFS mode of the SCALES Data Reduction Pipeline (SCALES-DRP) using recent laboratory results. SCALES (Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) is a thermal-infrared imager and integral-field spectrograph to be deployed on Keck II in late 2026, and will be the first facility-class, high-contrast IFS operating at 2–5 μm. The SCALES-DRP converts raw detector reads into three-dimensional IFS datacubes and implements optimal and χ² extraction to maximize signal-to-noise. The medium-resolution mode enables enhanced exoplanet characterization via a lenslet subarray (0.34 × 0.36 arcsec field of view) with an image slicer. Wavelength calibration and spectral extraction use rectification matrices derived from position-dependent lenslet PSFs measured with monochromatic calibration sources. We present laboratory results focusing on rectification performance and spectral extraction accuracy and robustness.

Items.Authors: Mackenzie R. Lach, Steph Sallum, Andrew Skemer, Athira Unni, Ravinder Banyal, Amirul Hasan, Arun Surya, William Deich, Daren Dillon, Renate Kupke, Nicholas MacDonald, Dusty Reichwein, Deno Stelter
Items.Title: Verifying the performance of the SCALES calibration unit
Items.Abstract: SCALES (Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) is an integral field spectrograph at W. M. Keck Observatory that will directly image young exoplanets and spectroscopically characterize their atmospheres from 2-5μm. Accurate calibration of SCALES is required in order to spectrally resolve atmospheric constituents. To achieve this, a calibration unit will be shipped to Keck alongside SCALES. This unit consists of a monochromator and a telescope simulator optics assembly. Preliminary testing of the calibration unit, paired with a spare NIRC2 filter and conducted at room temperature, indicated a small offset in monochromator wavelength. Such an offset does not pose problems for accurate calibration as long as it is well-known. We conduct additional testing of the calibration unit alongside the cooled SCALES detector and filters to verify its performance under realistic operating conditions and to measure the monochromator wavelength offset more precisely.

Items.Authors: Ajaykumar Dakshinamurthy, Sven Herrmann, Peter Orel, Anna-Katharina Schweingruber, Sebastian Albrecht, Astrid Mayr, Jonas Reiffers, Johannes Müller-Seidlitz, Steven W. Allen, Glenn Morris
Items.Title: VERITAS 2.3.1: optimisation and characterisation of the enhanced readout ASIC for the NewAthena Wide Field Imager
Items.Abstract: VERITAS 2.3.1 is the next step in the VErsatile Readout based on Integrated Trapezoidal Analog Shapers (VERITAS) integrated circuit (IC) architecture for high speed, low noise readout of Depleted field effect transistors (DEPFET) detectors in the Wide Field Imager (WFI) on ESA’s NewAthena X ray satellite. Functionality and performance characterization of VERITAS 2.3.1 were carried out using a dedicated application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) test setup, a hybrid test setup is used to perform measurements with DEPFET sensors under vacuum and mission-like temperature conditions. This paper presents the design updates and implementation details of VERITAS 2.3.1, compares its measured performance to that of VERITAS 2.3, and discusses the impact of the added features, block-level optimisations, and routing improvements on system behaviour.

Items.Authors: Yuki Hirose, Shuji Matsuura, Risa Hirose, Maiki Ebisu, Ryo Hashimoto, Takao Nakagawa, Shunsuke Nakagawa, Yusuke Ofuji, Yuki Ohara, Akimasa Ojika, Kei Sano, Aoi Takahashi, Kohji Takimoto, Hayato Tanaka, Yuto Tome, Akane Tsumoto, Kohji Tsumura
Items.Title: VERTECS: pre-flight performance of the optical multi-band camera module
Items.Abstract: VERTECS is a CubeSat designed to study the Extragalactic Background Light (EBL). We conducted pre-flight performance tests of the optical multi-band camera module installed in VERTECS. The camera module uses a commercially available CMOS sensor controlled by a custom-made image capture board. The sensor temperature is maintained below 0°C by the radiator during the observation in orbit. Through the tests, the detectability of the EBL was assessed while considering radiation effects. The detector noise evaluation showed that the detector noise was dominated by readout noise below 0°C, and the shot noise due to zodiacal light dominates over the detector noise in most observation sky regions. By comparing the noise during the observation with the signal electron count by the EBL estimated through the spectral responsivity evaluation, it was demonstrated that VERTECS can detect the EBL with the sufficient signal-to-noise ratio.

Items.Authors: Akimasa Ojika, Ryo Hashimoto, Yuki Ohara, Akane Tsumoto, Maiki Ebisu, Yuki Hirose, Risa Hirose, Yusuke Ofuji, Shuji Matsuura, Yuto Tome, Shunsuke Nakagawa, Kei Sano, Kohji Takimoto, Aoi Takahashi, Takao Nakagawa, Kohji Tsumura
Items.Title: VERTECS: PSF modeling using a 3D-CNN-Initialized Phase Diversity Method
Items.Abstract: VERTECS is a compact visible-light astronomical imaging satellite designed to measure the extragalactic background light (EBL). Accurate EBL estimation requires precise foreground light removal, which in turn demands a PSF model that varies smoothly across the field and remains stable under temperature changes. However, VERTECS’s fast F/2 telescope produces undersampled PSFs, making conventional wavefront-sensing methods unreliable. We developed a two-stage approach that combines a 3D convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) with phase-diversity (PD) optimization. The 3D-CNN provides robust initial estimates of eight primary Zernike coefficients from through-focus images, enabling PD to avoid local minima and converge reliably. The resulting field-dependent, temperature-parameterized wavefront model reproduces laboratory PSFs and supports accurate foreground light removal for VERTECS’s EBL measurement. Details of the simulation techniques are presented in the poster.

Items.Authors: Thomas L. Hayward, Andrew J. Adamson, Heather M. Carr, Logan Sato, Myung Cho, Charles Cavedoni, Peter Byrnes
Items.Title: Vibration characterization of the Gemini Telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present the results of a vibration study conducted by the International Gemini Observatory of its two telescopes on Maunakea, Hawaii, and Cerro Pachón, Chile. Modal exciter tests confirm the telescope structure and mirror cell vibration modes predicted by Finite-Element Analysis, and reveal the actual resonant frequencies and Frequency Response Functions. In particular, our tests confirm the presence of mirror cell tilt modes near 12 Hz suspected to be excited by the cryocoolers of the GNIRS instrument, and show that reducing the drive frequency by about 20% would avoid the resonance. We also measured the FRF near 60 Hz, the cryocooler drive frequency of forthcoming facility instruments, and telescope vibrations induced by cooling fans and instrument cryocoolers. Designers of forthcoming facility instruments are using these data to model both the effects of the telescope vibrations on their systems and the effects of their cryocoolers on the telescope.

Items.Authors: Paolo Turri, Friedrich Wöger, Luke Johnson, David Harrington, Brialyn Onodera, Stacey Sueoka, Dirk Schmidt, David Boboltz, Thomas Rimmele
Items.Title: Vibration measurements and effects on instrumentation performance at DKIST
Items.Abstract: The management of vibrations is crucial for the operation of large ground telescopes that use of adaptive optics systems. The diffraction-limited point spread function that is demanded from these optical systems can be ruined easily by small oscillations of many of the optical surfaces and sensors. Uncontrolled vibrations have hence the potential to blur the data of the scientific instruments, causing the loss of spatial resolution in the data. At the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST), we have measured and analyzed the vibrations that affect the quality of the scientific output of the telescope. We have combined the measurements from different types of sensors—accelerometer, imaging camera, and wavefront sensor—to characterize the frequency, amplitude and location of outstanding vibrations. The wavefront sensor telemetry has been analyzed also to investigate the oscillations on the adaptive optics bench of optical aberrations other than the tip-tilt of the focal plane.

Items.Authors: Shawn Barbod, Andy Adamson, Thomas L. Hayward, Ruben Diaz
Items.Title: Vibration requirements, characterization and mitigation approaches for 8-10 m class telescopes: an overview from the International Gemini Observatory
Items.Abstract: This paper provides an overview of how vibration requirements are defined and applied at the Gemini Observatory and other 8–10 m class telescopes. We summarize Gemini’s current vibration characterization efforts, including recent measurements, the emerging facility vibration profile, and planned future work. The paper highlights key opportunities and challenges from both operational and instrumentation perspectives, with attention to the needs of vibration-sensitive systems. We also outline mitigation strategies implemented at the observatory level and the approaches being adopted by upcoming projects such as GNAO and GIRMOS. The goal is to provide a practical reference for observatories and instrument teams working with vibration-critical instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Aysun Soenmez, Valeria Antonelli, Benjamin Mican, Jan Philipp Möller, Kurt Dittrich, Andreas Lederhuber, Walter Bornemann, Jonas Reiffers, Daniel Schuppe, Fabio Waldhör
Items.Title: Vibration testing of the Detector Electronics Unit (DEU) for the WFI instrument
Items.Abstract: The NewAthena mission’s Wide Field Imager (WFI) requires highly reliable detector electronics to ensure uninterrupted scientific performance during launch and operation. Functioning as the primary mechanical and electrical backbone of the WFI signal chain, the Detector Electronics Unit (DEU) must undergo early testing to ensure its robustness under launch conditions. To this end, a dedicated Mechanical Breadboard Vibration Test campaign was undertaken to replicate launch-representative vibration loads. The evaluation focused on the integrity of the mechanical, soldered, and glued joints, as well as the survivability of the Daisy Chain FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) interconnections, which represent one of the most critical links within the subsystem. Successful completion of the test provides confidence in the DEU architecture and supports progression towards full qualification in the current project phase.

Items.Authors: Miles Lucas, Laird Close, Jared Males, Tiago Gualberto Bezerra de Souza, Rodrigo Pereira, Jialin Li, Joseph D. Long, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Olivier Guyon, Alexander D. Hedglen, Parker T. Johnson, Maggie Kautz, Jay K. Kueny, Rico Landman, Joshua Liberman, Jennifer Lumbres, Matthijs Mars, Eden McEwen, Avalon L. McLeod, Kyle J. Van Gorkom, Lauren Schatz, Elena Tonucci, Katie Twitchell, Alycia J. Weinberger
Items.Title: Visible-light high-contrast polarimetric imaging with MagAO-X: characterization and early results
Items.Abstract: We present the characterization and on-sky results of the new polarimetric mode for the Magellan Extreme Adaptive Optics instrument MagAO-X at the 6.5 m Magellan Clay Telescope. The polarimetric mode enables dual-beam imaging polarimetry at r, i, and z filters using a switching HWP for instrumental polarization control. We will present lab characterization and on-sky observations of polarized standard stars to determine the polarimetric accuracy and precision of the Magellan Clay Telescope and MagAO-X. We will also present circumstellar disk images as a demonstration of the mode. We will discuss prospects for optimal polarimetry based on this characterization and its applications to future instruments, such as GMagAO-X and PCS.

Items.Authors: Salvatore Savarese, Laurent Marty, Mirko Colapietro, Pietro Schipani, Simone Di Filippo, Gabriele Umbriaco, Jacopo Farinato, Demetrio Magrin, Francesco Perrotta, Sergio D'Orsi, Giulio Capasso, Stefano Covino
Items.Title: VSTPOL: Progress on the Instrument Control Software for the New Polarimetric Mode
Items.Abstract: VSTPOL adds a new polarimetric capability to the VST by introducing a linear polarizing filter in place of the unused ADC, enabling the first large wide-field survey telescope with optical polarimetry and supporting applications such as optical follow-up of CTA sources. The mode requires two motorized motions: inserting the filter and rotating it to set the polarization angle and track the field.  To integrate modern PLC-based hardware while preserving compatibility with the existing VST software, a secondary Instrument Control Software (ICS) has been developed on a separate workstation running an updated VLT Software release. This environment manages the PLC devices and decouples the new control logic from the operational system.  The ICS has been tested with laboratory hardware and later with the realized VSTPOL sub system. A clone of the VST workstation was also reproduced to integrate the ICS and verify its behaviour under conditions matching those at the telescope.

Items.Authors: Andrés Asensio Ramos, Luzma Montoya, Nicolás Adrián Rodríguez-Linares, Yolanda Martin Hernando, Carlos Quintero Noda, Noelia Feijóo, Miguel Núñez Cagigal
Items.Title: Wavefront sensing and image quality assessment in solar AO
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) systems usually measure their performance using the Strehl ratio, a parameter derived from point-like stars. This approach cannot be applied to solar telescopes, since the Sun has no point sources in the image, making Strehl impossible to measure during regular observations. At the same time, solar AO relies on correlating WFS that requires a minimum FoV to operate, which introduces a fundamental wavefront error due to anisoplanatism.  In this work, we explore a new wavefront sensing technique based on neural networks that can better estimate the atmospheric distortions across the solar image, minimising the anisoplanatism effect. We compare its performance using traditional metrics and introduce an alternative image-quality indicator, the Median Filter Gradient Similarity (MFGS). All tests are performed with SAOS, a new solar AO simulator developed for the EST project.

Items.Authors: Tao Wang, Yonghui Hou, Teng Xu, Wei Wei, Chao Liu, Changyu Zeng, Yue Sun
Items.Title: Wavefront tip-tilt correction for faint target in unit telescope of long-baseline optical interferometer
Items.Abstract: In ground based long-baseline optical interferometer, the optical performance of the unit telescope is limited mainly by wavefront tilt errors from atmospheric turbulence and system disturbances, which becomes worse for faint targets. Within XuYi 100m long-baseline interferometer, We develop a faint-source-robust tilt-sensing method based on connected-region detection, weighted centroids, and spatial filtering techniques. Experiments show that the method effectively corrects wavefront tilt for weak targets and provides supports for high-precision interferometry.

Items.Authors: Serena Farina, Julian Lennox Canepa, Chiara Botta, Angelo Gulinatti, Andrea Bianco, Michela Uslenghi, Giovanni Pareschi
Items.Title: WAVE-SENSE: a large-area and buttable NUV detector based on wavelength shifters and SiPMs
Items.Abstract: We present the development of a large-area, buttable NUV detector based on wavelength-shifting (WLS) materials coupled to SiPMs. Incoming NUV photons are shifted to longer wavelengths and guided by reflective walls toward a SiPM placed behind the WLS slab, enabling four-sided buttability and the realization of large-format, pixelated arrays. This architecture provides a large effective collection area while reducing the total dark count rate compared to full-SiPM coverage. We summarize the detector design and characterize its WLS and SiPM components, and present preliminary results from the complete device along with planned next steps.

Items.Authors: Joseph D. Long, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Jared R. Males, Laird M. Close, Olivier Guyon, Lauren Schatz, Kyle Van Gorkom, Alexander D. Hedglen, Maggie Y. Kautz, Jay K. Kueny, Eden A. McEwen, Katie Twitchell, Joshua Liberman, Parker T. Johnson, Miles Lucas, Elena Tonucci, Matthijs Mars, Rico Landman
Items.Title: What the speck is that? Improving exoplanet imaging sensitivity by combining machine learning and physical models
Items.Abstract: Extreme adaptive optics observations of exoplanetary systems are limited at the smallest separations by speckle noise introduced by diffractive effects in the telescope and instrument system. To probe for lower-mass planets on close orbits, we need to improve starlight suppression with both optics and post-processing techniques. The promise of neural networks as universal function approximators led us to investigate their ability to predict a time-evolving point-spread function (PSF) from instrument telemetry (e.g. wavefront sensor data). By combining a physical optics model with a flexible machine learning model, we can avoid introducing unphysical features in the resulting PSF estimate. To make effective use of 2-3.7 kHz wavefront sensor data in analyzing science images taken at 5-10 Hz, we explore the temporal coherence of structures in our telemetry and the limitations of learning this relationship from data sampled on such different timescales.

Items.Authors: Marcel Loose
Items.Title: Workflow orchestration for pipelines that produce advanced data products (ADP)
Items.Abstract: Modern pipelines for producing advanced data products (ADP) are very complex. Both the workflow with its many conditional steps and loops, and the algorithms used to calculate the intermediate results.    By using the well-known architectural design pattern Pipes and Filters, we can properly separate the workflow description from the calculation details. The workflow describes inputs and outputs, the pipes. How inputs are forged into outputs is the responsiblity of the filters. This separation of concerns is both important for maintainability of the software, and for being able to efficiently execute a given workflow on the available compute resources.    Almost a decade ago, ASTRON decided to use the Common Workflow Language to describe the complex pipeline workflows. In this presentation I will dive into the experiences we have gained and the lessons we have learned.

Items.Authors: Matteo Ferro, Matteo Genoni, Jose Schiappacasse, Henri Boffin, Alessio Mucciarelli, Carmela Lardo, Cristian Vignali, Michele Ennio Maria Moresco, Margherita Talia, Roland Bacon, Roelof de Jong, Vincenzo Mainieri, Maria Sofia Randich, Marco Landoni, Andrea Scaudo
Items.Title: WST instrument exposure time calculator: full simulation of multi-mode spectrograph performance from source to detector
Items.Abstract: We present an Exposure Time Calculator for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope concept, simulating photon propagation from astronomical sources to detectors. WST features three spectroscopic modes: Integral Field Spectrograph (3700-9800Å, R3500), high-resolution Multi-Object Spectrograph (four bands, R40000), and low-resolution Multi-Object Spectrograph (three channels, R~3500). The ETC incorporates wavelength-dependent system throughput, accurate sky background modeling, and comprehensive noise treatment. It supports diverse target types (stellar templates, blackbody, power-law, emission lines) and spatial morphologies (point sources, Sersic profiles). Four calculation modes enable exposure time optimization for target SNR requirements. Outputs include wavelength-dependent SNR, photon counts, noise decomposition, and simulated spectra, enabling accurate predictions for proposal preparation and survey design through an interactive web interface.

Items.Authors: Paolo Calabretto, Claudio Labanti, Enrico Virgilli, Lorenzo Amati, Riccardo Campana, Giulia Mattioli, Smiriti Srivastava, Ezequiel J. Marchesini, Edoardo Borciani, Ajay Sharma, Giovanni La Rosa, Paolo Nogara, Giuseppe Sottile, Alfonso Pisapia
Items.Title: XGIS readout logic for photon-background discrimination and particle classification
Items.Abstract: The X and Gamma rays Imaging Spectrometer (XGIS) on board the THESEUS mission is a modular, finely pixelized instrument designed for broadband detection of high-energy transients. Each Camera hosts 10 SuperModules, subdivided into Modules with 64 Silicon Drift Detector pixels coupled to CsI scintillator bars. Based on recent simulations, we present the development of an optimized readout algorithm capable of quickly reading signals from all pixels and transmitting them in temporal order through the Module, SuperModule, and Camera logic. A key challenge for space-based high-energy detectors is background rejection without a dedicated anticoincidence system. We introduce a strategy exploiting spatial and temporal energy-deposit patterns, including energy–multiplicity thresholds and topology-based filters to implement in the readout system, and a feasibility study for an on-board particle-track classifier at Camera level.

Items.Authors: Henk J. van Weers
Items.Title: X-IFU focal plane assembly development model 1.1 realization and technology development status
Items.Abstract: Over the last two years a FPA development model update has been realized. A flight-like detector is included. Several new technologies have been developed, which are needed for the interconnections of this detector with subsequent electronics. In collaboration with CERN the Niobium magnetic shield has been redesigned. High-density wire-bonding is demonstrated. Developments are in progress to demonstrate flight-scalable super-conducting flex cables. Vibration tests have been performed on two detector stages and mechanical vibration levels are derived at sub-system level. This paper describes the integration results and includes an outlook of demonstrations foreseen up to adoption.

Items.Authors: Beverly J. LaMarr, Marshall W. Bautz, Eric D. Miller, Gregory Y. Prigozhin, Jill Juneau, Michelle Gabutti, Sven Herrmann, Peter Orel, Declan O'Neill, Tanmoy Chattopadhyay, Haley R. Stueber, Abigail Y. Pan, R. Glenn Morris, Steven W. Allen, Christopher Leitz, Mike Cooper, Kevan Donlon, Noah Pestana, Ilya Prigozhin, David Volfson, Keith Warner, Doug Young, Catherine E. Grant
Items.Title: X-ray characterization of large-format, 16-channel CCD sensors for AXIS
Items.Abstract: The Advanced X-ray Imaging Satellite (AXIS), an NASA Probe class mission now under Phase A study, requires high-frame-rate, low-noise, megapixel X-ray sensors. As part of a collaborative effort to develop the AXIS High-Speed Camera, MIT and Stanford University have been working to develop focal plane sensors that meet AXIS requirements. We have developed a form/fit/function prototype detector for AXIS, denoted the CCID100. The large-format (2 megapixel), 16-channel, charge coupled device, was designed and fabricated at MIT Lincoln Laboratory. Here we report results on characterization of the CCID100 sensors obtained at the MIT Kavli Institute. A front illuminated version has been tested from room temperature to -110C at readout speeds exceeding 10 frames per second. We describe the test setup and operating point tuning processes involved in examining the spectral performance, and its variation amongst output nodes, at energies from 700eV to 6keV.

Items.Authors: Bernard Kozioziemski, Lahsen Assoufid, Simon Bandler, Megan E. Eckart, Phillip Hamilton, XianRong Huang, Maurice Leutenegger, Edward E. Magee, Takashi Okajima, Wayne C. Stolte, Harrison Flores-Alimboyoguen
Items.Title: X-ray monochromators for calibration of the NewAthena X-ray Integral Field Unit transition-edge sensors
Items.Abstract: The X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) instrument on NewAthena features an array of transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeters, enabling high-resolution, energy-resolved X-ray imaging of astronomical objects. The X-IFU array is designed to achieve a sensor-level resolution requirement of 2.15 eV FWHM at energies up to 7 keV and 4 eV FWHM up to 10 keV. Calibration and performance testing requires narrow-linewidth X-ray sources that span a similar energy range to measure the detector line-spread function. These calibration measurements must be performed with a relatively low count rate of approximately one photon per second, necessitating simultaneous illumination of a large fraction of the array for efficient calibration. We present the design and initial testing of both in-air and in-vacuum X-ray monochromators with <1 eV FWHM linewidth. Our approach includes channel-cut crystals and flat crystals configured in a four-bounce geometry to cover the low-energy part of the waveband.

Items.Authors: Vadim Burwitz, Gisela Hartner, Thomas Müller, Surangkhana Rukdee, Thomas Schmidt, Giuseppe Vacanti, Maximilien Collon, Adam Lassise, Marcos Bavdaz
Items.Title: X-ray parallel beam measurements of NewATHENA silicon pore optics at PANTER
Items.Abstract: The ESA NewATHENA X-ray observatory is slated for mission adoption in 2027 and launch in the late 2030s. NewATHENA features a 2.5 m diameter and 12 m focal length X-ray Mirror Assembly (XMA) that supports up to 600 Silicon Pore Optic (SPO) mirror modules (MMs). The PANTER X-ray test facility has been key to this process of characterising the SPO MMs. Usually, the TMMs are characterised using the divergent beam with the X-ray source located at 120 m from the X-ray optic. A new setup at PANTER has been implemented using a Fresnel zone plate to produce a parallel X-ray beam that can fully illuminate a SPO MM. The results of divergent and parallel beam measurements of a calibration master mirror module MM-0037 composed of a primary and a secondary silicon mandrel, and the first NewATHENA flight-like SPO MM-0058 will be presented.

Items.Authors: Giorgio Savini, Enzo Pascale, José Antonio Araiza-Durán, Andrea Bocchieri, Paolo Chioetto, Anna Brucalassi, Martin Caldwell, Stavros Misopoulos, Salma Fahmy, Piotr Wawer, Grzegorz Szymanski, Anne Philippon, Benoit Lecomte, Yannis Argyriou Tsikrikonis
Items.Title: Zemax macro-enabled pan-chromatic and dynamic PSF simulations for Fine Guidance Sensor spot modelling
Items.Abstract: This paper aims to present a simple way of using outputs of Zemax raytracing to improve prediction of the point spread function of space telescope outputs on Fine Guidance Sensors. This is done both to evaluate changes caused by different spectral type stars as well as variations potentially caused by known models of pointing jitter.   Macros in ZPL language can easily be coded to provide ray incidence on a given surface at a variety of wavelengths and field positions. This provides a reference grid in which a separate accurate pointing model can navigate by switching to the nearest neighbour spot and produce for a given integration time the resulting spot cloud at the detector.  This code procedure also aims to facilitate and optimise of the M2 mirror positioning on the Ariel satellite telescope during Commissioning phase.

Items.Authors: Prakriti Gupta, Yashvi Sharma, John I. Bailey
Items.Title: ZShooter: ScopeSim and early DRP prototyping to enhance design
Items.Abstract: We are building a ZShooter‑specific extension of the ScopeSim instrument‑simulation framework and coupling it to existing open‑source echelle pipelines such as PyReduce and PypeIt. This end‑to‑end setup produces realistic detector‑level frames for the three‑arm ZSpec spectrograph and tri‑band ZImager camera and immediately feeds them into prototype reduction recipes. Here we will demonstrate how this approach lets a small team explore performance trades, observing strategies, and calibration plans very early in the design, while simultaneously de‑risking the future data‑reduction pipeline and quick‑look tools.

Items.Authors: Nicholas E. White, Massimiliano Galeazzi, Daniel Kocevski, Jon E. Grove, Sylvain Guiriec, Alexander J. van der Horst, Russell Roberts, Brendan O'Connor, Paul S. Ray, Dheeraj Pasham, Peter Roming
Items.Title: XTRA: The X-ray TRansient Array
Items.Abstract: XTRA (X-ray TRansient Array) is a NASA Small Explorer concept designed for 2030s time-domain and multi-messenger astrophysics. Operating in a Sun-Earth L2 orbit, XTRA makes time-domain surveys and provides rapid autonomous response to high-energy transients. The payload combines the Burst Alert Monitor (BAM)—a broadband (50 keV–2 MeV) gamma-ray monitor for continuous triggering—with the Micropore Optics X-ray Instrument (MOXI)—a wide-field (240 sq deg) soft X-ray (0.2–5 keV) imager for rapid arcminute localization. Surveying the anti-Sun nighttime hemisphere on a variety of cadences, XTRA acts as the high-energy anchor for the 2030s ecosystem, feeding triggers to robotic telescopes for immediate counterpart identification. XTRA will decode cosmic explosions (GRBs, shock breakouts), trace black hole feeding via tidal disruption events (TDEs), and uncover electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational wave and high-energy neutrino sources.

Items.Authors: Peter G. Tuthill
Items.Title: Astrometric detection of rocky exoplanets from inexpensive space platforms
Items.Abstract: The detection of exoplanets by way of astrometric monitoring of the host star to reveal gravitational reflex motion requires extreme precision in measurement stability for Earth-mass objects. Despite this, astrometry is widely regarded as the most promising technology for the most desired of all targets: true Earth analogues in the solar neighbourhood. Formerly thought to require flagship class investment, recently several smaller concepts such as the TOLIMAN and SHERA missions have shown that detections are possible, at least in principle, from more modest space platforms. A key enabling feature of these missions is narrow-angle astrometry: a binary star provides its own astrometric reference greatly alleviating problems from using distant, faint field stars. However, few nearby star systems are multiple. This paper advances novel optical concepts featuring ultra-stable telescopes of modest (<0.5m) aperture for micro-arcsecond monitoring of isolated single stars.
